Very unprofessional. I made an appointment. When I showed up at the allotted time, there was a backlog of four people with what looked like at least an hour wait. Everybody can fall behind schedule. I think everyone can sympathize with that. But give people the courtesy of a call so they don’t waste their time. When you don’t, it gives people the message “my time is more valuable than yours.”

The following is a response to your reply (I see no option to reply otherwise). First, thanks for taking the time to reply. The fact that I was 10 minutes late in this instance simply meant I would have waited even longer given the doctor was behind schedule, hence why I didn't mention it. More to the point, my "excessive assumption" was in fact not an assumption at all. When the doctor told me a 15 minute wait and I saw the four people waiting in the room, I explicitly asked the doctor if all of these people were waiting because if so it didn't seem like it would be 15 minutes. She explicitly said yes all of these people were waiting. When I said that would clearly be more than 15 minutes she just said "I'm sorry I'm behind schedule." Assuming 15 minutes per person to estimate an hour wait time was a reasonable assumption based on what I saw and what the doctor told me, not an exaggeration.

Now I take you at your word and assume good intentions that she simply didn't understand me, but it's important to note based on what I saw and what the doctor told me there was no reason to assume this would be a relatively short, 15 minute wait.

Again, falling behind schedule is something we can all sympathize with. But a call to a patient, or even just a text, if you're going to be excessively late would be courteous (there was a receptionist there). If I'm going to be late or if the doctor is late give or take 10 minutes it's not a big deal. But close to half an hour is a different story. If I were going to be half an hour late I would certainly have called. I'm sure your patients would appreciate this as well if you fall behind schedule again.

It was one mistake. It happens. Best of luck going forward.
